title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos were created and distributed using the faces of Dutch public figures including celebrities, politicians, and members of the Royal Family without their consent. The videos appeared on a platform with approximately 13 million monthly visitors. This represents a failure of content moderation, where a system deployed at scale did not prevent the creation or hosting of illegal material.

The deployment lacked adequate safeguards against synthetic media abuse. The system appears to have operated without meaningful human review or automated detection of non-consensual intimate imagery before images reached a mass audience. What would have caught this was either human review of content before publication, detection systems trained to identify deepfake pornography, or verification that individuals had consented to their likenesses being used.

It is not established how the deepfake videos were created, whether they were generated using a single tool or multiple methods, or what technical measures the hosting platform employed to detect or prevent such content.

summary:
Multiple female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in manipulated pornographic videos. These videos appear on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors and feature numerous Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, and members of the Royal Family. The interim Justice Minister has called the videos abhorrent and urged victims to file complaints. Several victims have confirmed they have already filed reports or are exploring legal options.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's face is digitally placed onto adult performers, falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore illegal. Legal experts advise victims to file complaints with police, potentially leading to website shutdowns. Other options include launching group lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. This follows a previous case where television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma successfully prosecuted a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort who received a conditional sentence of 180 hours for creating fake pornographic videos of her.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
